descriptions.s3: Buckets of Amazon S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi and more.
descriptions.gcs: Buckets of Google Cloud, with an HMAC key.
descriptions.gdrive: My Drive or a shared drive of a Google account.

catalog.title: What do you want to connect to?
catalog.description: Choose the kind of server or storage. Only the ones this instance offers are listed.

keep: Leave blank to keep the stored one.

reasons.host: Enter a host name or address, without scheme, port or path.
reasons.timezone: Choose a time zone of the list.
reasons.unknown: This setting is not part of this kind of server.
reasons.secret: This setting is a secret and is sent apart.

choices.optional: Use explicit FTP over TLS if available

notes.explicit: Starts in clear text and upgrades with AUTH TLS before signing in; a server that does not offer TLS is refused. The first time, its certificate is shown for you to confirm.
notes.implicit: Speaks TLS from the first byte, usually on port 990. The first time, the server's certificate is shown for you to confirm.

warnings.optional: If the server does not offer TLS, or someone on the network removes the offer, the password and the files go in clear text without a warning. Prefer requiring TLS.
warnings.plain: FTP sends the password and the files without encryption. Use TLS if the server offers it.

notes.anonymous: Signs in as anonymous with no secret saved, as public servers expect. An SFTP server is first asked to let it in without authentication.
notes.ask: No password is saved. It is asked for when connecting and kept only in the server's memory for your session.
notes.interactive: No secret is saved. Whatever the server asks when connecting, the password or a one-time code, is asked to you then and never kept.
notes.account: Some older FTP servers ask for an account after the password (ACCT). It is kept in the vault like the password.

password.label: Password
password.keep: Leave blank to keep the existing password.

account.label: Account
account.keep: Leave blank to keep the existing account.

list_timezone.label: Server time zone
list_timezone.hint: The time zone the server lists times in. Most servers use UTC.

charset.label: Character set of file names
charset.hint: Change it only for old servers that show accents wrong; most servers use UTF-8.

proxy_kind.label: Proxy
proxy_kind.hint: Tunnels the connection through a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy instead of connecting directly.

jump_host.label: Jump host
jump_host.hint: Tunnels the SSH connection through this server first, as ssh -J does. Leave the host blank to connect directly.

tls.label: Use HTTPS
tls.hint: Encrypts the keys and the files on their way to the service.

warnings.false: Without HTTPS the access key signature and the files travel in clear text. Turn it off only for a service on your own network.

region.label: Region
region.hint: Leave it blank and AWS finds the region of the bucket; other services may need one, such as auto for Cloudflare R2.

bucket.label: Bucket
bucket.hint: The bucket the site opens; its folders are the prefixes of its keys.

secret_access_key.label: Secret access key
secret_access_key.keep: Leave blank to keep the stored secret access key.

shared_drive.label: Shared drive
shared_drive.hint: Leave it blank to open My Drive, or give the name of a shared drive of the account.

refresh_token.label: Google account
refresh_token.hint: Signs in with Google in a new window. Only a token that lets Transferly reach Drive is kept, sealed in the vault; the password never reaches Transferly.

container.label: Container
container.hint: The container the site opens; its folders are the prefixes of its blob names.

share.label: Share
share.hint: The file share the site opens.

account_key.label: Account key
account_key.keep: Leave blank to keep the stored account key.

sas_token.label: SAS token
sas_token.hint: The query string of a shared access signature, with or without the leading question mark.
sas_token.keep: Leave blank to keep the stored SAS token.

path.label: Path
path.hint: The folder on the server the site opens, such as /remote.php/dav/files/alice/ on Nextcloud.

sudo.label: Use sudo
sudo.hint: Runs the SFTP server of the host through sudo, so the site reads and writes as another user, root by default. Only admins may turn it on, and commands on servers must be allowed.

sudo_password.label: Sudo password
sudo_password.hint: What sudo asks for. Leave it empty to answer with the password of the account, or when sudo asks for none.
sudo_password.keep: Leave blank to keep the saved sudo password.

host.label: Endpoint
host.hint: s3.amazonaws.com for AWS, or the host of the service: MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze B2 and the like.

notes.access_key: Signs every request with the access key. The secret access key is sealed in the vault.
notes.anonymous: Reads a public bucket without signing the requests; nothing is saved.

host.label: Endpoint
host.hint: storage.googleapis.com. Change it only for a private gateway.

bucket.hint: The Cloud Storage bucket the site opens; its folders are the prefixes of its object names.

access_key_id.label: HMAC access ID
access_key_id.hint: Create an HMAC key in Cloud Storage → Settings → Interoperability.

secret_access_key.label: HMAC secret
secret_access_key.keep: Leave blank to keep the stored HMAC secret.

notes.access_key: Signs every request with the HMAC key. The secret is sealed in the vault.
notes.anonymous: Reads a public bucket without signing the requests; nothing is saved.

host.label: Endpoint
host.hint: Leave it blank for Azure. Give the host of a sovereign cloud, such as account.blob.core.chinacloudapi.cn, or of an emulator such as Azurite.

notes.account_key: Signs every request with the key of the whole storage account, sealed in the vault. A SAS token with only the permissions the site needs is safer.
notes.sas: Authorizes the requests with a shared access signature, limited to what it grants and until it expires. Sealed in the vault.
notes.anonymous: Reads a container of public access without signing the requests; nothing is saved.

account.label: Storage account
account.hint: The name of the storage account, as in account.blob.core.windows.net.

host.label: Endpoint
host.hint: Leave it blank for Azure. Give the host of a sovereign cloud, such as account.blob.core.chinacloudapi.cn, or of an emulator such as Azurite.

notes.account_key: Signs every request with the key of the whole storage account, sealed in the vault. A SAS token with only the permissions the site needs is safer.
notes.sas: Authorizes the requests with a shared access signature, limited to what it grants and until it expires. Sealed in the vault.
notes.anonymous: Reads a container of public access without signing the requests; nothing is saved.

account.label: Storage account
account.hint: The name of the storage account, as in account.blob.core.windows.net.

host.label: Server
host.hint: The name or address of the WebDAV server, without https:// nor a path.

tls.hint: Encrypts the password and the files on their way to the server. A self-signed certificate is shown to you to trust, as for FTPS.

warnings.false: Without HTTPS the password and the files travel in clear text. Turn it off only for a server on your own network.

notes.password: Signs in with HTTP Basic authentication. The password is sealed in the vault.
notes.anonymous: Opens a public share without signing in; nothing is saved.

oauth.waiting: Waiting for Google… finish signing in the window that opened.

failures.denied: Google did not grant access. Try again and allow Transferly to see and manage your Drive files.
failures.expired: The sign-in took too long or was already used. Try again.
failures.no_refresh_token: Google signed in without giving a lasting token. Remove Transferly from the third-party access of the account and try again.
failures.not_configured: Signing in with Google is not set up on this instance. Ask an administrator.
failures.failed: Signing in with Google failed. Try again.
failures.blocked: The browser blocked the window of Google. Allow pop-ups for Transferly and try again.
